issue: The same VIN appears in more than one sale record, representing used-vehicle resale.
handling: Preserved repeated VINs and added additional used-sale history; do not treat VIN as a unique sale key.

issue: Service visit customer/contact details may identify the person who brought the vehicle, not necessarily its registered owner.
handling: Preserved visit contact fields and DMS customer references; resolve vehicle ownership periods separately before routing service history or alerts.

issue: The same person may appear at multiple dealerships with different DMS customer numbers, spelling, ID formatting or contact details.
handling: Preserved cross-source variations; use identity resolution cautiously and avoid automatic merges based on shared vehicle alone.

issue: Detected 240 chronological mileage decreases between adjacent retained service visits for the same VIN (date parsing based on available date formats).
handling: Retained these values as source-quality examples; profile and flag them in transformations rather than silently correcting source data.

issue: Timestamp formats vary in the prepared file; generated rows deliberately retain multiple formats for normalization testing.
handling: Preserve raw timestamp and create a normalized timestamp during ingestion/transformation; validate ambiguous day/month values.

issue: A vehicle's owner changes over time; current owner cannot be inferred from VIN alone or from the latest service visitor.
handling: Retained repeated VIN sale history and added sale records with dates; model ownership start/end periods and determine current owner from latest valid sale.

issue: Company customer records represent fleet entities, while employees may be vehicle drivers or workshop visitors.
handling: Retained all company/fleet customer master records in the 4,500-row selection; keep company and person identities distinct.

issue: Rows added to meet target counts are synthetic extensions based on mentor-source patterns.
handling: Generated contact IDs use CON-SYN-, lead IDs use LEAD-SYN-, sale IDs use SALE-SYN-, and email event IDs use EV-SYN-. Treat these as prepared training data, not new mentor-provided facts.
